title: GameStop vs. eBay: When a Retailer Bets Big on a Hostile Takeover
hook: GameStop, the video game retailer that became famous as a meme stock, is now pursuing a takeover of one of the world's biggest e-commerce platforms. eBay said no. GameStop is pressing on anyway.
background: GameStop is an American brick-and-mortar (physical store) retailer that has historically sold video games, consoles, and electronics. It became globally famous in 2021 when retail investors drove its share price to extraordinary heights in what became known as the "meme stock" phenomenon. eBay is a major American e-commerce marketplace where millions of buyers and sellers transact online, competing with platforms such as Amazon and Etsy.
what_happened: GameStop made a takeover offer to acquire eBay, signalling a dramatic strategic pivot away from physical retail.
eBay's board rejected the offer, indicating it did not believe the bid reflected adequate value or strategic fit.
GameStop publicly announced it would pursue the takeover regardless of the rejection, making the bid hostile in nature.

title: Pride or Profit? How DEI Retreats Are Reshaping LGBTQ+ Consumer Spending
hook: Target, Walmart, and Amazon built loyalty with millions of LGBTQ+ shoppers. Now, a single policy shift may be costing them billions. When companies quietly roll back diversity commitments, do consumers quietly walk away?
background: Target, Walmart, and Amazon are three of the largest retailers in the United States, together serving hundreds of millions of customers annually across physical stores and e-commerce platforms. For years, all three publicly championed diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) initiatives, which are company policies designed to support underrepresented groups in the workplace and in marketing. Beginning around 2025, each company scaled back visible DEI commitments, decisions that coincided with a broader political pressure campaign against corporate diversity programmes.
what_happened: A 2026 survey by the Human Rights Campaign (HRC), a major LGBTQ+ advocacy organisation, found that LGBTQ+ consumers were actively redirecting their spending away from retailers perceived as retreating on DEI.
Target, Walmart, and Amazon were among the brands most frequently cited by respondents as having lost their trust and purchasing loyalty.
Respondents indicated they were favouring competitors and smaller brands they viewed as maintaining or strengthening their commitments to LGBTQ+ inclusion.

title: SpaceX Goes Public: The $75 Billion Question
hook: In June 2026, SpaceX pulled off the largest public offering in history, raising $75 billion in a single stock market debut. For a company that spent years insisting it had no need for public markets, that is quite a turnaround.
background: SpaceX, founded by Elon Musk in 2002, is an aerospace manufacturer and space transportation company headquartered in California. It builds rockets, operates satellite internet through its Starlink network, and has secured major contracts with NASA and the US Department of Defense. By 2026, it had also expanded into artificial intelligence, making it one of the most complex and closely watched private companies in the world.
what_happened: SpaceX launched its initial public offering (IPO) on the Nasdaq stock exchange in June 2026, trading under the ticker symbol SPCX.
The IPO raised $75 billion, surpassing all previous records for a public offering and valuing the company at approximately $1.78 trillion.
The listing gave ordinary investors, for the first time, the ability to buy shares in a company that had previously only been accessible to private investors and venture capital funds.

title: Eli Manning Bought Youth Sports. Congress Wants to Take It Back.
hook: A two-time Super Bowl winner walks into a private equity deal. It sounds like the start of a joke, but for Eli Manning and his Brand Velocity Group, acquiring youth sports licensor RCX is a serious strategic move, made at exactly the moment politicians are trying to ban it.
background: Brand Velocity Group (BVG) is a private equity firm co-founded by NFL legend Eli Manning that acquires and grows consumer brands. RCX Sports is the company that holds the licence to organise and commercialise NFL Flag football, the non-contact, youth-oriented version of American football played by millions of children across the United States. Private equity refers to investment firms that buy companies using a combination of investor funds and debt, with the goal of growing and eventually selling them at a profit.
what_happened: Brand Velocity Group announced a deal to acquire RCX Sports, the licensing company behind NFL Flag football programmes.
The acquisition gives BVG control over the commercial rights to one of the fastest-growing youth sports in the United States.
The deal was announced while a bill was moving through the US Congress that would restrict or ban private equity ownership in youth sports organisations.

title: Inside Information or Just Being Smart? The Polymarket Insider Trading Test
hook: A Google engineer allegedly turned his employer's secret data into $1.2 million in trading profits. Now a landmark legal case is asking a question nobody has answered yet: can you commit insider trading on a prediction market?
background: Polymarket is an online prediction market where users bet real money on the outcomes of future events, from elections to economic data releases. Google is one of the world's largest technology companies, whose search engine processes billions of queries daily, generating vast internal data about what people are searching for in real time. That internal data, known as search trend data, is proprietary, meaning it belongs to Google and is not available to the public.
what_happened: A Google engineer was arrested in May 2025, accused of accessing confidential internal search trend data to predict the outcomes of events listed on Polymarket.
The engineer allegedly used those predictions to place trades on Polymarket, accumulating profits of approximately $1.2 million.
Prosecutors argued this constituted insider trading, the illegal practice of trading on material, non-public information that gives one party an unfair advantage over others.

title: To the Moon: But Who Pays? SpaceX's IPO and the Price of a Vision
hook: SpaceX wants to raise more money from public investors than almost any company in history. The catch? It is still losing money. So why would anyone buy in?
background: SpaceX (Space Exploration Technologies Corp.) is an American aerospace company founded in 2002 by Elon Musk with the stated goal of making humanity a multi-planetary species. It designs, manufactures, and launches rockets and spacecraft, most notably the Falcon 9 and the Starship rocket. Beyond rockets, SpaceX operates Starlink, a commercial satellite internet service that beams broadband connectivity to customers in remote areas worldwide using a vast constellation of low-orbit satellites. SpaceX has historically been a private company, meaning its shares are not available for ordinary members of the public to buy on a stock exchange.
what_happened: SpaceX is planning an Initial Public Offering (IPO) -- the first time a private company sells shares to the general public on a stock exchange -- that could raise approximately $75 billion, potentially making it the largest IPO in history.
The company intends to use the funds raised to finance its most ambitious missions, including a return to the Moon and an eventual crewed mission to Mars.
Starlink, SpaceX's satellite internet division, has become a significant and growing source of revenue, providing the company's strongest financial performance.
